beats.care: Hyderabad's pharma belt employs many young chemists and supervisors. Workplace safety rules exist for a reason; ask about them.
beats.what: Two employees of Saraca Laboratories in Gaddapotharam, Jinnaram mandal, died after inhaling chloroform vapours late on Thursday.
beats.why: The leak happened while chloroform was moved from a first-floor reactor to a ground-floor receiver. Vapours spread fast.

cards.body: The victims, a chemist and a supervisor aged 44 and 27, were from Andhra Pradesh. The Telangana Pollution Control Board ordered the unit closed and its power disconnected.
It's a solvent used in making medicines. Breathing in high amounts in a closed space can cause unconsciousness and death.
cards.title: why is chloroform dangerous?

opts: Ordered the unit shut and power cut
cards.q: What action did the Pollution Control Board take?
cards.why: TGPCB ordered immediate closure and disconnection of electricity.

hook: Chemical leak at a pharma unit near Hyderabad leaves *two workers* dead

learn.t: Telangana's Sangareddy and Medak districts host one of India's biggest bulk drug manufacturing clusters.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Two killed in chloroform vapour leak at pharma unit (print, Hyderabad edition, 24 Oct, p.1)

tldr: Two employees died after chloroform vapour leaked at a pharma plant in Sangareddy district. The unit has been shut.
watch: Watch for an inquiry report on safety lapses at the unit.
